note: SHORT #2 out of the 8:23 interview, and deliberately NOT a reshuffle of EDEN HER STORY - it uses a stretch that film never touches (5:47-7:07). The subject is HIS reaction, which is the hook: he has never met anyone with cancer before, and he says so. Then the turn - 'a few years ago you were like me' - then the line the whole short exists for: 'Eden, do you understand how strong you are?' Her answer is a shake of the head, so it carries NO caption: in Hebrew her 'lo' agrees with him, in English 'NO' would read as contradiction. Ends on her own prescription - go up, believe, smile - not on the V9 closer. autoFrame OFF; xc per beat. FRAMING, v4: the source is ALREADY 9:16 (1920x1080 with rotation), so `crop=1080:1920` removes nothing and the per-beat `xc` was inert - every beat came out as the same locked wide, faces a tenth of the frame with the bottom half a duvet. The only lever that does anything here is the zoompan push, so framing is {z,x,y} per beat. Measured off a gridded still at 352s: Tal's face x0.17 y0.44, Eden's x0.72 y0.45.
beats: HOOK. 'You are the first woman in my life I have met who has cancer. Did you know that?'
THE TURN. 'It touches my heart - a few years ago you were like me, healthy. One day everything changed, and you don't give up.'

THE LINE. 'But Eden, do you understand how strong you are? Really - think about it. You are surviving a disease and you don't give up.' (recovered by a targeted large-v3 pass; the whole-file transcript had 16s of nothing here)
HER ANSWER - a shake of the head. NO CAPTION, deliberately.
'You always have to -' 'Go up.' 'And to -' 'Believe.' 'And to -' 'Smile.' 'Always.'
'It makes me happy that you smile.'
THE CLOSER. 'You just have to smile, and believe, and that people will come and visit you and pray for you.'
